In à la carte service, cutlery is laid at the beginning of each course. Since customers order individual dishes one at a time, the appropriate cutlery for each course is brought and laid as that course is about to be served, rather than all at once.

The breakfast menu in which the service of fish and beef is most appropriate is full breakfast. A full breakfast (English breakfast) is a comprehensive morning meal that includes cooked items such as eggs, bacon, sausage, fish, and beef alongside bread, toast, and beverages.

The main function of a bain marie is keeping foods hot. A bain marie is a heated water bath used in professional kitchens to maintain cooked dishes at serving temperature. Food containers sit in or over the hot water, preventing cooling without overcooking.

The area of study that specialises on provision of foods and drinks is catering. Catering is the field of study and practice concerned with the preparation, presentation, and service of food and beverages to customers in various settings.

When a restaurant predicts its expected guest count based on room count, it is known as guest forecasting. Guest forecasting uses hotel occupancy data (number of rooms booked) to predict how many guests will use the restaurant, enabling appropriate staffing and food preparation.

The type of menu that offers the same dishes every day is a static menu. A static menu remains constant over a long period with the same selection available daily. It suits establishments with a fixed, loyal customer base — fast food restaurants, diners, or pubs.

Anchovy is a type of oily fish. Anchovies are small, flavourful salt-water fish high in omega-3 fatty acids and oils throughout their flesh, classifying them as oily fish alongside sardines, mackerel, and herring.

According to the answer key, transferring bacteria from contaminated to uncontaminated foods via hands is known as food poisoning. (Note: the standard term for this process is cross-contamination; food poisoning is the illness that may result. Follow the given key: A.)

A kitchen equipment that could be used for toasting and baking is an oven. An oven provides enclosed dry heat suitable for baking breads, cakes, and pastries, as well as for toasting bread and gratinating dishes with a top heat element.

Sommelier is also referred to as the wine waiter. The sommelier is a trained wine professional who manages the wine list, advises guests on wine selection and food-wine pairings, and is responsible for presenting and serving wine in the restaurant.

The culinary term 'pané' (pane) means floured, egged, and crumbed — the standard breadcrumbing process. Food is first coated in flour (to provide a dry surface), then dipped in beaten egg (as an adhesive), then coated in breadcrumbs before frying.

The term that describes the thickness of a flour mixture is consistency. Consistency refers to the degree of thickness or viscosity of a batter, dough, or sauce — ranging from thin/liquid to thick/stiff. Getting the right consistency is critical in baking and cooking.

A burn is an accident caused by hot iron (a hot dry surface or object). Burns are caused by contact with hot dry surfaces — irons, ovens, hot pans, flames. This distinguishes burns from scalds, which are caused by hot liquids or steam.

Lamb is a rich source of protein. As a red meat, lamb provides high-quality complete protein containing all essential amino acids, as well as iron, zinc, and B vitamins (particularly B12 and niacin) — essential nutrients for growth and repair.

Another name for a hot cupboard is a hot plate. A hot cupboard/hot plate is a heated storage unit used to keep cooked food and plates warm at serving temperature until they are ready to be taken to customers.

Venison refers to the meat of a deer. It is a lean, dark red game meat with a distinctive rich flavour. Venison is lower in fat and cholesterol than beef and is considered a healthy alternative to conventional red meats.

Hors d'oeuvre is another name for the first course. 'Hors d'oeuvre' is a French term meaning 'outside the work' — referring to the appetiser course served before the main meal. It stimulates the appetite and sets the tone for the dining experience.

Caviar is obtained from sturgeon. Caviar consists of the salted roe (eggs) of the sturgeon fish, particularly Beluga, Ossetra, and Sevruga species. It is considered a luxury delicacy, prized for its distinctive briny, buttery flavour.

The difference between selling price and cost price of a dish is known as gross profit. Gross profit = Selling price − Cost price. It represents the profit before deducting labour and overhead costs, and is a key measure of dish profitability.

The unique features of à la carte menu include individual price and many choices. Each dish is priced separately, and the menu offers a wide variety of dishes from which customers can choose freely, creating a personalised dining experience.

In food and beverage establishments, safety rules must be observed by barmen, chefs, and stewards — all staff members. Safety is a universal obligation; every employee, regardless of their specific role, must adhere to health and safety regulations to protect themselves and others.

The meat obtained from old hens is usually tough. As poultry ages, the muscle fibres become more developed and connective tissue increases, making the meat tougher and less tender than meat from young birds (broilers).

The right procedure for making tea is to brew tea with boiling water. Boiling water (100°C) is essential for proper extraction of the tea's flavour compounds, colour, and beneficial properties. Water that is too cool produces a weak, inferior infusion.

To maintain a refrigerator at peak efficiency, it should be defrosted weekly. Regular defrosting removes ice build-up from the evaporator coils, which if allowed to accumulate, reduces cooling efficiency, increases energy consumption, and can cause mechanical strain.

The key characteristic of table d'hôte menu is that the waiting time is long. Since dishes are prepared fresh in sequence for each course, and all customers typically begin together, the multi-course format of table d'hôte results in longer dining times between courses.

Cash discount is allowed in consideration of credit patronage. A cash discount is offered to customers who pay promptly or on credit account terms, rewarding those who patronise the establishment on credit and settle their accounts regularly.

A cover is incomplete without a spoon. A dining cover (complete place setting for one person) must include at minimum a knife, fork, and spoon. The spoon is essential for soups, desserts, and beverages, completing the basic cover.

Kitchen windows should be screened to prevent entry of insects. Insects (flies, mosquitoes, cockroaches) carry disease-causing microorganisms that can contaminate food. Window screens act as physical barriers, keeping the kitchen pest-free and hygienic.

Languages used in the menu should be simple so that guests can comprehend it fully. Clear, straightforward menu language enables all customers to understand what is being offered, regardless of their education or language background, facilitating easy ordering.

The catering industry consists of tangible and intangible elements such as food, drinks, and atmosphere. Tangible elements (physical food and beverages) are complemented by intangible elements (ambiance, service quality, atmosphere) that together constitute the complete catering experience.

A waiter should serve food to guests from the right side with the right hand. This is the standard service convention — serving from the right prevents reaching across guests, respects personal space, and maintains a professional, fluid service style.

When planning a menu for pregnant women, it is important to avoid the use of alcohol. Alcohol consumption during pregnancy is dangerous — it crosses the placenta, affecting the developing foetus and potentially causing foetal alcohol syndrome and other developmental problems.

Fresh wounds must be covered with bandage. A bandage holds the dressing securely over the wound, applying gentle pressure to control bleeding and keeping the wound clean and protected. In a food handling context, a waterproof cover is placed underneath.

For a hospitality industry to flourish, the most important operational combination is skilled labour and capital. Skilled workers (trained chefs, managers, service staff) combined with adequate financial capital enable high-quality service delivery and sustainable business operations.

The major vitamin in citrus fruit is Vitamin C (ascorbic acid). Citrus fruits (oranges, lemons, limes, tangerines, grapefruit) are exceptionally rich in Vitamin C, which supports immune function, collagen synthesis, and iron absorption.

As a cleaning and maintenance procedure, most kitchen equipment requires brushing and polishing. Brushing removes food deposits, grease, and debris from surfaces and joints; polishing restores the shine and protective surface of stainless steel and other metals.

The operation of the hospitality industry in Nigeria began with the arrival of missionaries. European missionaries established rest houses (mission houses) along their travel routes to provide accommodation and food, laying the foundation for Nigeria's hospitality industry.

During microwave cooking, food is cooked wholly at the centre (from the inside out). Microwaves penetrate food and cause water molecules to vibrate, generating heat internally. The cooking starts at the centre and spreads outward, unlike conventional cooking which heats from the outside.

The personnel who prepares and serves cocktails is known as a wine butler. (Note: in standard practice, a mixologist or bartender prepares cocktails; a wine butler manages wine service. The answer key specifies wine butler — follow accordingly: B.)

In a fire outbreak, you should not use lifts (elevators). In emergencies, lifts can fail, trap occupants, or open directly onto fire floors. Evacuees must always use fire escape stairways, keeping lifts free for emergency services.

Entertainment is not a segment of the hospitality industry in this context. The main segments of the hospitality industry are: Accommodation, Food and Beverage, and Travel and Tourism. Entertainment is a leisure/recreation sector, separate from the core hospitality segments.
